brief: Goldman's Oct 7 equities recap: indices fell modestly (S&P -22bps to 7,801, NDX -21bps, Russell -131bps, Dow -66bps) with defensive posturing under the hood (NDX>SPX>RTY) as global yields kept backing up, pushing the cyclicals-vs-defensives pair -159bps. Small caps underperformed NDX for a 4th straight day on rates pain, though a strong $39bn 10-year auction (1.6bps through) offered some relief. Desk activity was muted (4 of 10), net -630bps for sale. Shawn Tuteja flagged that overall positioning stays low, but prime-book net exposure to the Magnificent Seven is near 22% of total US exposure, a record since 2022, while semis exposure sits at ~12%, down from a June peak of 14%. September brought the largest tech buying in a month since Feb '25. Costco's August comps (+11.4% total, +8% US ex-gas/FX) were solid but at the lower end of +8-9% expectations. In derivatives, little panic showed despite the pullback: vol was offered, skew bid, XLF saw 1-3m upside buyers, and the desk called gamma cheap after today's move realized to the downside. Tomorrow's straddle is 41bps. Financials earnings start next Tuesday (JPM, C, WFC) after the sector's worst September since 1999, though Q4 has historically favored it.
